children.text: In the opening sequence of this video, the rhetor establishes credibility by stating her credentials “a soon to be second-year medical student at Harvard.” Since Harvard is considered the number one medical school in America and a regarded Ivy League school, the prestige of the institution may grab the attention of viewers who are aware of this. She speaks in a very calm voice, immediately revealing the content of the video, which displays her “Day in my Life,” a popular type of trend video on TikTok. Because the “Day in my Life” videos are generally favored by viewers, the algorithm may promote this video to a wider audience outside of her regular follower count. Along with this voiceover, she includes video content that follows the traditional style of the “Day in my Life” trend, including making her bed and beginning a morning skincare routine.

The rhetor displays clips of herself putting makeup on, which is a common video clip to include in “Day in my Life” or “Get Ready with Me” videos. Users who are interested in achieving the beauty standard and a similar look to the influencer may be interested in her makeup routine and the products that she generally uses. She employs platform affordances by linking these products on her shop my in a folder called “makeup routine:),” linked in her TikTok bio. Ethical implications come into play here, because although she is promoting non-medical products her position as a medical student may imply scientific validation that does not exist. In addition, the medical field is a largely general profession that encompasses much of modern life, so it is difficult to define a hard line between medical and non-medical products. For example, skincare and cosmetics may be implicated under the umbrella of dermatology.

Towards the end of the video Melissa alludes to the future, referring to “some exciting upcoming projects.” This direct reference to the future while being covert about the subject encourages followers to stay engaged with her content, or non-followers to follow her in order to see what these future projects entail. With this voiceover, she displays video content of her working on a computer in fast motion with a listed time frame of about two hours. This marketing strategy targets human curiosity by leaving an information gap to trigger followers to wonder what it will be, causing them to feel a greater, more exclusive connection to her by knowing that she is working on an upcoming project that will be revealed to all viewers in the future.

At the very end of the video, Melissa displays her wind-down nighttime routine, stating “by now I was exhausted.” She gives specific products features via short video clips, including Amika haircare and Tatcha moisturizer. By including them in her nighttime routine, she implies that these products help her unwind and go to sleep, encouraging the audience to purchase these products if they want the same wind-down experience. She utilizes platform affordances by listing these Amika shampoo and conditioner on her shop my in a folder called “hair care,” linked in her TikTok bio. These products are also included in her Amazon Storefront in a folder called “Hair Essentials,” also linked in her TikTok bio. Ethical implications may be considered here for the same reasons as listed above.

Qin communicates a sense of authenticity by incorporating humor and sarcasm into her voiceover. She makes the statement “I literally landed less than 24 hours ago, so this is me trying to get my life together.” This use of verbiage makes her appear more relatable to young viewers, most likely students within the healthcare field with packed schedules. Anyone who has just returned from vacation, especially an audience that may fit this description, has felt the sense of urgency to get back to their daily life and attend to what they have missed while being away. The use of the phrase “getting my life together” also alludes to a popular aesthetic throughout internet culture, which idolizes organization, routines, and productivity.

The creator continues to build her authenticity of this video by showcasing herself to be a normal person, without extravagant routines or luxuries all of the time. She shows her meal for breakfast, noting “Oats were all I had so that was my breakfast.” This messaging contradicts a lifestyle that many influencers showcase, with elaborate meals aimed at promoting health and wellness. While this meal is still healthy, it is simple and plain, portraying Melissa as a “normal” individual who does not always have time to go grocery shopping and make breakfast. Her audience of busy students within the healthcare field may find this meal more relatable and practical than other meals including fruits and vegetables and large sources of proteins, which can be expensive and time-consuming to cook.

In this portion of the video, Melissa creates a sense of connection and familiarity with her audience. She mentions working in research related to public health, “which many of you know that I minored in in college.” This statement indicates that she is aware her audience knows her life experiences well, and that she doesn’t need to repeatedly communicate this information with them. This casual comment reinforces the transparasocial relationship between Melissa and her audience. By not only acknowledging them but indicating that they should know personal details about her, she creates a feeling of mutual camaraderie. While her audience may know her well, she likely does not know them, but attempts to diminish any feelings of parasociality with this comment. During this audio, she displays herself putting on designer items in an outfit for a day in the lab, reinforcing the idea that she is an organized and put together individual.

Melissa includes some of the companies of products she has clipped tagged in the caption of her TikTok. Most of these tags are hidden unless you click the “more” button next to the caption. In an earlier video clip, you can see her unboxed PR packages, some including these products. By giving these products screentime, Melissa is advertising PR that has been sent to her without directly stating this. I would argue that although this type of covert advertisement may cause newer viewers to question her authenticity, an audience that has followed her for a long time would choose to overlook this. As a creator, Melissa has explicitly stated multiple times that she uses the money she makes from TikTok to pay for her medical school tuition. An audience of students who are considering or already going into a vast amount of debt to pay for a medical education would be more understanding towards brand partnerships, with a “get that bag” mentality rather than feeling upset by this. However, the perceived purpose of the video may shift from educational or entertainment more towards product promotion.
